head: Era
Role of hypothermic circulatory arrest
rows: **Essential** for neonatal arch reconstruction and many complex neonatal operations; **reasonable** for most complex operations on full-term neonates and infants; **unreasonable** for simple operations and most complex operations in older infants and children (unless arch reconstruction)

stem: Two criteria are used to judge continuous full-body CPB and continuous ACP against hypothermic circulatory arrest in neonates and infants. What is the **current status** of these criteria according to the source?

Brain protection is confirmed; equal technical outcomes are unresolved
Neither is met, so HCA remains essential for arch reconstruction
Technical equivalence is confirmed; brain protection is unresolved

explanation.text: Criterion 1 (==technical outcomes==) is **met**; criterion 2 (==end-organ, especially brain, preservation==) is **complex, controversial and unresolved**.

head: Criterion
Status
rows: 1. Technical outcomes equal to or better than HCA
**Met**: all neonatal and infant operations, including arch reconstruction, can be done with continuous CPB (with continuous ACP when needed)
2. End-organ (brain) structure and function preserved as well or better

stem: Once CPB is established for **neonatal arch reconstruction using continuous ACP**, to what temperature and for how long is the patient cooled?

choices.text: 22°C to 24°C for at least 15 minutes
18°C to 20°C for at least 15 minutes
28°C to 30°C for at least 10 minutes
16°C to 18°C for at least 20 minutes
30°C to 32°C for at least 15 minutes

explanation.text: With continuous ACP, cool to ==22°C to 24°C for at least 15 minutes== to ensure **uniform cooling of the central nervous system**.

explanation.caption: Neonatal continuous ACP versus HCA cooling
head: Continuous ACP
Hypothermic circulatory arrest
rows: pH-stat or alpha-stat (pH-stat favored for neurologic outcome)

explanation.text: the patient is cooled to 22°C to 24°C for a minimum of 15 minutes to ensure uniform cooling of the central nervous system.
explanation.ref: Chapter 2: Hypothermia, Circulatory Arrest, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass, p. 81

choiceNotes.b: **18°C to 20°C** is where cooling stops in **adult** left thoracotomy distal arch surgery.
choiceNotes.c: The source cools to **22°C to 24°C** for a minimum of **15 minutes**.
choiceNotes.d: Nasopharyngeal **16°C–18°C** after **at least 20 minutes** of cooling is the guidance for **hypothermic circulatory arrest**.
choiceNotes.e: **30°C to 32°C** is what surface cooling usually reaches by the time CPB starts for HCA.

stem: During neonatal continuous ACP, the brachiocephalic, left carotid and left subclavian arteries are each clipped with **neurovascular clips**, isolating perfusion to the **head and right arm**. Which flow and acid-base strategy are then used?

choices.text: 40 mL/kg/min with pH-stat management
40 mL/kg/min with alpha-stat management
120 mL/kg/min with pH-stat management
200 mL/kg/min with alpha-stat management
10–15 mL/kg/min with alpha-stat management

explanation.text: With perfusion isolated to the head and right arm, flow is reduced to ==40 mL/kg/min== and acid-base management shifts to ==pH-stat==.

explanation.caption: Flow and acid-base through neonatal continuous ACP
head: Phase
CPB flow
Acid-base

explanation.text: Next the **ductus** is formally ligated and transected (as appropriate) and the mobilized **descending aorta is clamped distally**.
At this point, direct perfusion is isolated to the head and right arm, the flow rate is reduced to 40 mL · kg^-1^ · min^-1^, and acid-base management shifts to pH-stat.
explanation.ref: Chapter 2: Hypothermia, Circulatory Arrest, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass, p. 82

choiceNotes.b: Acid-base management **shifts to pH-stat** at this point; alpha-stat is used during cooling and rewarming.
choiceNotes.c: **120 mL/kg/min** is the flow after cooling, before the arch vessels are clipped.
choiceNotes.d: **200 mL/kg/min** with alpha-stat is used at the **start** of CPB and during **rewarming**.
choiceNotes.e: **10–15 mL/kg/min** is the **adult** standardized ACP flow.

stem: A neonate with arch hypoplasia and an **associated intracardiac lesion** is on continuous ACP, and the **arch reconstruction is completed**. Which is the **preferred** next step?

choices.text: Convert to hypothermic circulatory arrest for the intracardiac repair
Rewarm to normothermia, wean, and stage the intracardiac repair
Clamp the ascending aorta first, then release the descending clamp and clips
Repair the intracardiac lesion during continuous ACP before removing the clips
Remove the descending clamp and clips first, then clamp the ascending aorta

explanation.text: Preferred: ==restore total body perfusion first==, with a standard **ascending aortic clamp placed before** releasing the descending clamp and clips, then do the intracardiac repair.

branches.label: no
branches.text: Remove clamp and clips: total body perfusion **coincides** with myocardial reperfusion

branches.label: yes
branches.text: **Ascending aortic clamp first**, then remove descending clamp and clips

steps.text: Flow **120–150 mL/kg/min**; more cardioplegia as needed; intracardiac repair

explanation.text: Without remaining lesions, removing the clamp and clips **coincides with myocardial reperfusion**; with remaining lesions, the **ascending aortic clamp goes on first**.

If any remaining intracardiac lesions are present, a standard aortic clamp is placed on the ascending aorta before the descending aortic clamp and the neurovascular clips on the brachiocephalic arteries are removed.
explanation.ref: Chapter 2: Hypothermia, Circulatory Arrest, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass, p. 82

choiceNotes.a: The source restores **total body perfusion** at 120–150 mL/kg/min for the intracardiac repair.
choiceNotes.b: The intracardiac repair is done **in the same operation** after total body perfusion is restored.
choiceNotes.d: This is possible, but the **preferred** method is to restore **total body perfusion** first.
choiceNotes.e: The ascending aortic clamp goes on **before** the descending clamp and neurovascular clips are removed.

stem: After neonatal arch reconstruction using **brachiocephalic artery cannulation**, the patient is rewarmed to normothermia and weaned from CPB. What does the source stress about the **arterial cannula**?

choices.text: Remove it before rewarming, to restore native arterial flow
Remove it right after separation from CPB
Leave it in place for some hours as an arterial monitoring line
Keep it until chest closure, in case CPB must be resumed
Advance it into the reconstructed arch before weaning

explanation.text: Remove the arterial cannula from the brachiocephalic artery ==immediately after separation from CPB== to prevent **obstruction or arterial thrombosis**.

steps.text: Remove caval snares; IVC cannula back **up** into the right atrium
CPB flow increased to **200** (printed as mL · kg^-1^); rewarm with **alpha-stat**

explanation.text: To prevent obstruction or arterial thrombosis, it is important to remove the arterial cannula from the brachiocephalic artery immediately after separation from CPB.
explanation.ref: Chapter 2: Hypothermia, Circulatory Arrest, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass, p. 82

choiceNotes.a: CPB continues through it during **rewarming**; it is removed after separation from CPB.
choiceNotes.c: It is removed **immediately** after separation to prevent **obstruction or arterial thrombosis**.
choiceNotes.d: The source stresses removal **immediately** after separation from CPB.
choiceNotes.e: The cannula is never advanced beyond **2 mm**; it is removed after separation.
